transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, Bob, thank you for moderating tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Arizona State, for welcoming us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And thank you to the Presidential Commission for undertaking this enormous task.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re proud to be here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: President, I’m glad to be here with you again to share similarities and differences with the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Will we ever be safe and secure again?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We absolutely must be.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the goal.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, how do we achieve it is the most critical component of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe that this president, regrettably, rushed us into a war, made decisions about foreign policy, pushed alliances away.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And, as a result, America is now bearing this extraordinary burden where we are not as safe as we ought to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The measurement is not: Are we safer?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The measurement is: Are we as safe as we ought to be?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And there are a host of options that this president had available to him, like making sure that at all our ports in America containers are inspected.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Only 95 percent of them — 95 percent come in today uninspected.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not good enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: People who fly on airplanes today, the cargo hold is not X-rayed, but the baggage is.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not good enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Firehouses don’t have enough firefighters in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Police officers are being cut from the streets of America because the president decided to cut the COPS program.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So we can do a better job of homeland security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can do a better job of waging a smarter, more effective war on terror and guarantee that we will go after the terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will hunt them down, and we’ll kill them, we’ll capture them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’ll do whatever is necessary to be safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I pledge this to you, America: I will do it in the way that Franklin Roosevelt and Ronald Reagan and John Kennedy and others did, where we build the strongest alliances, where the world joins together, where we have the best intelligence and where we are able, ultimately, to be more safe and secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Bob, thank you very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank Arizona State as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we can be safe and secure, if we stay on the offense against the terrorists and if we spread freedom and liberty around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have got a comprehensive strategy to not only chase down the Al Qaida, wherever it exists — and we’re making progress; three-quarters of Al Qaida leaders have been brought to justice — but to make sure that countries that harbor terrorists are held to account.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a result of securing ourselves and ridding the Taliban out of Afghanistan, the Afghan people had elections this weekend.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the first voter was a 19-year-old woman.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Think about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Freedom is on the march.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We held to account a terrorist regime in Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In other words, in order to make sure we’re secure, there must be a comprehensive plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent just this weekend talked about how terrorism could be reduced to a nuisance, comparing it to prostitution, illegal gambling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that attitude and that point of view is dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think you can secure America for the long run if you don’t have a comprehensive view as to how to defeat these people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: At home, we’ll do everything we can to protect the homeland.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I signed the homeland security bill to better align our assets and resources.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing everything we can to protect our borders and ports.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But absolutely we can be secure in the long run.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It just takes good, strong leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: When the president had an opportunity to capture or kill Osama bin Laden, he took his focus off of them, outsourced the job to Afghan warlords, and Osama bin Laden escaped.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Six months after he said Osama bin Laden must be caught dead or alive, this president was asked, “Where is Osama bin Laden?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” He said, “I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t really think about him very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m not that concerned.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “ We need a president who stays deadly focused on the real war on terror.

transcript_turns.text: Gosh, I just don’t think I ever said I’m not worried about Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s kind of one of those exaggerations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’re worried about Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re on the hunt after Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re using every asset at our disposal to get Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.text: My opponent said this war is a matter of intelligence and law enforcement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, this war is a matter of using every asset at our disposal to keep the American people protected.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Bob, we relied upon a company out of England to provide about half of the flu vaccines for the United States citizen, and it turned out that the vaccine they were producing was contaminated.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we took the right action and didn’t allow contaminated medicine into our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re working with Canada to hopefully — that they’ll produce a — help us realize the vaccine necessary to make sure our citizens have got flu vaccinations during this upcoming season.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My call to our fellow Americans is if you’re healthy, if you’re younger, don’t get a flu shot this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Help us prioritize those who need to get the flu shot, the elderly and the young.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The CDC, responsible for health in the United States, is setting those priorities and is allocating the flu vaccine accordingly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t gotten a flu shot, and I don’t intend to because I want to make sure those who are most vulnerable get treated.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a problem with litigation in the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vaccine manufacturers are worried about getting sued, and therefore they have backed off from providing this kind of vaccine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons I’m such a strong believer in legal reform is so that people aren’t afraid of producing a product that is necessary for the health of our citizens and then end up getting sued in a court of law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the best thing we can do now, Bob, given the circumstances with the company in England is for those of us who are younger and healthy, don’t get a flu shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This really underscores the problem with the American health-care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s not working for the American family.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And it’s gotten worse under President Bush over the course of the last years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Five million Americans have lost their health insurance in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got about a million right here in Arizona, just shy, 950,000, who have no health insurance at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 82,000 Arizonians lost their health insurance under President Bush’s watch.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 223,000 kids in Arizona have no health insurance at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: All across our country — go to Ohio, 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 4 million Ohioans have no health insurance, 114,000 of them lost it under President Bush; Wisconsin, 82,000 Wisconsinites lost it under President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president has turned his back on the wellness of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And there is no system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In fact, it’s starting to fall apart not because of lawsuits — though they are a problem, and John Edwards and I are committed to fixing them — but because of the larger issue that we don’t cover Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Children across our country don’t have health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re the richest country on the face of the planet, the only industrialized nation in the world not to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to cover all Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to make it affordable and accessible.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to let everybody buy into the same health-care plan senators and congressmen give themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to remind people listening tonight that a plan is not a litany of complaints, and a plan is not to lay out programs that you can’t pay for.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He just said he wants everybody to be able to buy in to the same plan that senators and congressmen get.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That costs the government $7,700 per family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If every family in America signed up, like the senator suggested, if would cost us $5 trillion over 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an empty promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s called bait and switch.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Actually, it’s not an empty promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s really interesting, because the president used that very plan as a reason for seniors to accept his prescription drug plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He said, if it’s good enough for the congressmen and senators to have choice, seniors ought to have choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What we do is we have choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I choose Blue Cross/Blue Shield.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Other senators, other congressmen choose other programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But the fact is, we’re going to help Americans be able to buy into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Those that can afford it are going to buy in themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re not giving this away for nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you exactly how I can do it: by reinstating what President Bush took away, which is called pay as you go.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: During the 1990s, we had pay-as-you-go rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: If you were going to pass something in the Congress, you had to show where you are going to pay for it and how.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: President Bush has taken — he’s the only president in history to do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He’s also the only president in 72 years to lose jobs — 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 6 million jobs lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He’s the only president to have incomes of families go down for the last three years; the only president to see exports go down; the only president to see the lowest level of business investment in our country as it is today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’m going to reverse that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to change that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to restore the fiscal discipline we had in the 1990s.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Every plan that I have laid out — my health-care plan, my plan for education, my plan for kids to be able to get better college loans — I’ve shown exactly how I’m going to pay for those.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we start — we don’t do it exclusively — but we start by rolling back George Bush’s unaffordable tax cut for the wealthiest people, people earning more than $200,000 a year, and we pass, hopefully, the McCain-Kerry Commission which identified some $60 billion that we can get.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We shut the loophole which has American workers actually subsidizing the loss of their own job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They just passed an expansion of that loophole in the last few days: $43 billion of giveaways, including favors to the oil and gas industry and the people importing ceiling fans from China.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to stand up and fight for the American worker.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I am going to do it in a way that’s fiscally sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I show how I pay for the health care, how we pay for the education.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a manufacturing jobs credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We pay for it by shutting that loophole overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We raise the student loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I pay for it by changing the relationship with the banks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president has never once vetoed one bill; the first president in a hundred years not to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, his rhetoric doesn’t match his record.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He been a senator for 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He voted to increase taxes 98 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When they tried to reduce taxes, he voted against that 127 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talks about being a fiscal conservative, or fiscally sound, but he voted over — he voted 277 times to waive the budget caps, which would have cost the taxpayers $4.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 2 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talks about PAYGO.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you what PAYGO means, when you’re a senator from Massachusetts, when you’re a colleague of Ted Kennedy, pay go means: You pay, and he goes ahead and spends.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s proposed $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 2 trillion of new spending, and yet the so-called tax on the rich, which is also a tax on many small-business owners in America, raises $600 million by our account — billion, $800 billion by his account.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a tax gap.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And guess who usually ends up filling the tax gap?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I propose a detailed budget, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I sent up my budget man to the Congress, and he says, here’s how we’re going to reduce the deficit in half by five years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It requires pro-growth policies that grow our economy and fiscal sanity in the halls of Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d say, Bob, I’ve got policies to continue to grow our economy and create the jobs of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And here’s some help for you to go get an education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Here’s some help for you to go to a community college.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve expanded trade adjustment assistance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We want to help pay for you to gain the skills necessary to fill the jobs of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, there’s a lot of talk about how to keep the economy growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We talk about fiscal matters.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But perhaps the best way to keep jobs here in America and to keep this economy growing is to make sure our education system works.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I went to Washington to solve problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I saw a problem in the public education system in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They were just shuffling too many kids through the system, year after year, grade after grade, without learning the basics.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we said: Let’s raise the standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re spending more money, but let’s raise the standards and measure early and solve problems now, before it’s too late.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, education is how to help the person who’s lost a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Education is how to make sure we’ve got a workforce that’s productive and competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Got four more years, I’ve got more to do to continue to raise standards, to continue to reward teachers and school districts that are working, to emphasize math and science in the classrooms, to continue to expand Pell Grants to make sure that people have an opportunity to start their career with a college diploma.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so the person you talked to, I say, here’s some help, here’s some trade adjustment assistance money for you to go a community college in your neighborhood, a community college which is providing the skills necessary to fill the jobs of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I would say to that person.

transcript_turns.text: I want you to notice how the president switched away from jobs and started talking about education principally.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Let me come back in one moment to that, but I want to speak for a second, if I can, to what the president said about fiscal responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Being lectured by the president on fiscal responsibility is a little bit like Tony Soprano talking to me about law and order in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president has taken a $5.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 6 trillion surplus and turned it into deficits as far as the eye can see.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Health-care costs for the average American have gone up 64 percent; tuitions have gone up 35 percent; gasoline prices up 30 percent; Medicare premiums went up 17 percent a few days ago; prescription drugs are up 12 percent a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But guess what, America?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The wages of Americans have gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The jobs that are being created in Arizona right now are paying about $13,700 less than the jobs that we’re losing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the president just walks on by this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that he’s cut job-training money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: $1 billion was cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They only added a little bit back this year because it’s an election year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve cut the Pell Grants and the Perkins loans to help kids be able to go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve cut the training money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve wound up not even extending unemployment benefits and not even extending health care to those people who are unemployed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to do those things, because that’s what’s right in America: Help workers to transition in every respect.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t blame them entirely for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I blame the president for the things the president could do that has an impact on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Outsourcing is going to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve acknowledged that in union halls across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “And I’ve looked them in the eye and I’ve said, “No, I can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “ What I can promise you is that I will make the playing field as fair as possible, that I will, for instance, make certain that with respect to the tax system that you as a worker in America are not subsidizing the loss of your job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Today, if you’re an American business, you actually get a benefit for going overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You get to defer your taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So if you’re looking at a competitive world, you say to yourself, “Hey, I do better overseas than I do here in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “ That’s not smart.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want American workers subsidizing the loss of their own job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And when I’m president, we’re going to shut that loophole in a nanosecond and we’re going to use that money to lower corporate tax rates in America for all corporations, 5 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to have a manufacturing jobs credit and a job hiring credit so we actually help people be able to hire here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The second thing that we can do is provide a fair trade playing field.

transcript_turns.text: This president didn’t stand up for Boeing when Airbus was violating international rules and subsidies.

transcript_turns.text: He discovered Boeing during the course of this campaign after I’d been talking about it for months.

transcript_turns.text: The fact is that the president had an opportunity to stand up and take on China for currency manipulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that there have been markets shut to us that we haven’t stood up and fought for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to fight for a fair trade playing field for the American worker.

transcript_turns.text: And I will fight for the American worker just as hard as I fight for my own job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry

transcript_turns.text: The Lewin report is a group of folks who are not politically affiliated.

transcript_turns.text: They analyzed the senator’s plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It cost $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 2 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Lewin report accurately noted that there are going to be 20 million people, over 20 million people added to government-controlled health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It would be the largest increase in government health care ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you raise the Medicaid to 300 percent, it provides an incentive for small businesses not to provide private insurance to their employees.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Why should they insure somebody when the government’s going to insure it for them?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s estimated that 8 million people will go from private insurance to government insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a fundamental difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think government- run health will lead to poor-quality health, will lead to rationing, will lead to less choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Once a health-care program ends up in a line item in the federal government budget, it leads to more controls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And just look at other countries that have tried to have federally controlled health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They have poor-quality health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our health-care system is the envy of the world because we believe in making sure that the decisions are made by doctors and patients, not by officials in the nation’s capital.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president just said that government-run health care results in poor quality.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, maybe that explains why he hasn’t fully funded the VA and the VA hospital is having trouble and veterans are complaining.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Maybe that explains why Medicare patients are complaining about being pushed off of Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He doesn’t adequately fund it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But let me just say to America: I am not proposing a government-run program.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have Blue Cross/Blue Shield.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Senators and congressmen have a wide choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Americans ought to have it too.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Talk about the VA: We’ve increased VA funding by $22 billion in the four years since I’ve been president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s twice the amount that my predecessor increased VA funding.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’re meeting our obligation to our veterans, and the veterans know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re expanding veterans’ health care throughout the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re aligning facilities where the veterans live now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Veterans are getting very good health care under my administration, and they will continue to do so during the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First, let me make sure that every senior listening today understands that when we’re talking about reforming Social Security, that they’ll still get their checks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember the 2000 campaign, people said if George W.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: gets elected, your check will be taken away.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, people got their checks, and they’ll continue to get their checks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a problem for our youngsters, a real problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if we don’t act today, the problem will be valued in the trillions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I think we need to think differently.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll honor our commitment to our seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But for our children and our grandchildren, we need to have a different strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And recognizing that, I called together a group of our fellow citizens to study the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a committee chaired by the late Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan of New York, a Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they came up with a variety of ideas for people to look at.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that younger workers ought to be allowed to take some of their own money and put it in a personal savings account, because I understand that they need to get better rates of return than the rates of return being given in the current Social Security trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the compounding rate of interest effect will make it more likely that the Social Security system is solvent for our children and our grandchildren.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I will work with Republicans and Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’ll be a vital issue in my second term.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is an issue that I am willing to take on, and so I’ll bring Republicans and Democrats together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re of course going to have to consider the costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I want to warn my fellow citizens: The cost of doing nothing, the cost of saying the current system is OK, far exceeds the costs of trying to make sure we save the system for our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You just heard the president say that young people ought to be able to take money out of Social Security and put it in their own accounts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, my fellow Americans, that’s an invitation to disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The CBO said very clearly that if you were to adopt the president’s plan, there would be a $2 trillion hole in Social Security, because today’s workers pay in to the system for today’s retirees.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the CBO said — that’s the Congressional Budget Office; it’s bipartisan — they said that there would have to be a cut in benefits of 25 percent to 40 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, the president has never explained to America, ever, hasn’t done it tonight, where does the transitional money, that $2 trillion, come from?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He’s already got $3 trillion, according to The Washington Post, of expenses that he’s put on the line from his convention and the promises of this campaign, none of which are paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Not one of them are paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that the president is driving the largest deficits in American history.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He’s broken the pay-as-you-go rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a record of fighting for fiscal responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In 1985, I was one of the first Democrats — broke with my party.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We balanced the budget in the ’90s.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We paid down the debt for two years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we’re going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to protect Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will not privatize it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will not cut the benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to be fiscally responsible.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we will take care of Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Not at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This is the same thing we heard — remember, I appeared on “Meet the Press” with Tim Russert in 1990-something.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We heard the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We fixed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In fact, we put together a $5.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 6 trillion surplus in the ’90s that was for the purpose of saving Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: If you take the tax cut that the president of the United States has given — President Bush gave to Americans in the top 1 percent of America — just that tax cut that went to the top 1 percent of America would have saved Social Security until the year 2075.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president decided to give it to the wealthiest Americans in a tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, Alan Greenspan, who I think has done a terrific job in monetary policy, supports the president’s tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I support it for the middle class, not that part of it that goes to people earning more than $200,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And when I roll it back and we invest in the things that I have talked about to move our economy, we’re going to grow sufficiently, it would begin to cut the deficit in half, and we get back to where we were at the end of the 1990s when we balanced the budget and paid down the debt of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, we can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, if later on after a period of time we find that Social Security is in trouble, we’ll pull together the top experts of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’ll do exactly what we did in the 1990s.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll make whatever adjustment is necessary.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But the first and most important thing is to start creating jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The jobs the president is creating pay $9,000 less than the jobs that we’re losing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And this is the first president in 72 years to preside over an economy in America that has lost jobs, 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 6 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Eleven other presidents — six Democrats and five Republicans — had wars, had recessions, had great difficulties; none of them lost jobs the way this president has.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to put America back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And if we’re fiscally responsible and put America back to work, we’re going to fix Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He forgot to tell you he voted to tax Social Security benefits more than one time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t hear any plan to fix Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I heard more of the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talks about middle-class tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly where the tax cuts went.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Most of the tax cuts went to low- and middle-income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now the tax code is more fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Twenty percent of the upper-income people pay about 80 percent of the taxes in America today because of how we structured the tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People listening out there know the benefits of the tax cuts we passed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you have a child, you got tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re married, you got tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you pay any tax at all, you got tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All of which was opposed by my opponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the tax relief was important to spur consumption and investment to get us out of this recession.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People need to remember: Six months prior to my arrival, the stock market started to go down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it was one of the largest declines in our history.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then we had a recession and we got attacked, which cost us 1 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we acted.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I led the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We passed tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now this economy is growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We added 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 9 million new jobs over the last 13 months.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sure, there’s more work to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the way to make sure our economy grows is not to raise taxes on small-business owners.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not to increase the scope of the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s to make sure we have fiscal sanity and keep taxes low.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see it as a serious problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see it as a security issue, I see it as an economic issue, and I see it as a human-rights issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re increasing the border security of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got 1,000 more Border Patrol agents on the southern border.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re using new equipment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re using unmanned vehicles to spot people coming across.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll continue to do so over the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a subject I’m very familiar with.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: After all, I was a border governor for a while.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Many people are coming to this country for economic reasons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re coming here to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you can make 50 cents in the heart of Mexico, for example, or make $5 here in America, $5.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 15, you’re going to come here if you’re worth your salt, if you want to put food on the table for your families.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what’s happening.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so in order to take pressure off the borders, in order to make the borders more secure, I believe there ought to be a temporary worker card that allows a willing worker and a willing employer to mate up, so long as there’s not an American willing to do that job, to join up in order to be able to fulfill the employers’ needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That has the benefit of making sure our employers aren’t breaking the law as they try to fill their workforce needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It makes sure that the people coming across the border are humanely treated, that they’re not kept in the shadows of our society, that they’re able to go back and forth to see their families.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See, the card, it’ll have a period of time attached to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It also means it takes pressure off the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If somebody is coming here to work with a card, it means they’re not going to have to sneak across the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It means our border patrol will be more likely to be able to focus on doing their job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s very important for our citizens to also know that I don’t believe we ought to have amnesty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we ought to reward illegal behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are plenty of people standing in line to become a citizen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we ought not to crowd these people ahead of them in line.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If they want to become a citizen, they can stand in line, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And here is where my opponent and I differ.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In September 2003, he supported amnesty for illegal aliens.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Let me just answer one part of the last question quickly, and then I’ll come to immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The American middle-class family isn’t making it right now, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And what the president said about the tax cuts has been wiped out by the increase in health care, the increase in gasoline, the increase in tuitions, the increase in prescription drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is, the take-home pay of a typical American family as a share of national income is lower than it’s been since 1929.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the take-home pay of the richest .

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 1 percent of Americans is the highest it’s been since 1928.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Under President Bush, the middle class has seen their tax burden go up and the wealthiest’s tax burden has gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now that’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, with respect to immigration reform, the president broke his promise on immigration reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He said he would reform it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Four years later he is now promising another plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Here’s what I’ll do: Number one, the borders are more leaking today than they were before 9/11.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is, we haven’t done what we need to do to toughen up our borders, and I will.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we need a guest-worker program, but if it’s all we have, it’s not going to solve the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The second thing we need is to crack down on illegal hiring.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s against the law in the United States to hire people illegally, and we ought to be enforcing that law properly.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And thirdly, we need an earned-legalization program for people who have been here for a long time, stayed out of trouble, got a job, paid their taxes, and their kids are American.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We got to start moving them toward full citizenship, out of the shadows.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: SCHIEFFER: Do you want to respond, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: President?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, to say that the borders are not as protected as they were prior to September the 11th shows he doesn’t know the borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re much better protected today than they were when I was the governor of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have much more manpower and much more equipment there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He just doesn’t understand how the borders work, evidently, to say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is an outrageous claim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll continue to protect our borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re continuing to increase manpower and equipment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Four thousand people a day are coming across the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that we now have people from the Middle East, allegedly, coming across the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re not doing what we ought to do in terms of the technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have iris-identification technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have thumbprint, fingerprint technology today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can know who the people are, that they’re really the people they say they are when they cross the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We could speed it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: There are huge delays.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The fact is our borders are not as secure as they ought to be, and I’ll make them secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m glad you raised that question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s long overdue time to raise the minimum wage.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And, America, this is one of those issues that separates the president and myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have fought to try to raise the minimum wage in the last years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But the Republican leadership of the House and Senate won’t even let us have a vote on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re not allowed to vote on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want to raise the minimum wage.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The minimum wage is the lowest minimum wage value it has been in our nation in 50 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: If we raise the minimum wage, which I will do over several years to $7 an hour, 9.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 2 million women who are trying to raise their families would earn another $3,800 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president has denied 9.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: 2 million women $3,800 a year, but he doesn’t hesitate to fight for $136,000 to a millionaire.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: One percent of America got $89 billion last year in a tax cut, but people working hard, playing by the rules, trying to take care of their kids, family values, that we’re supposed to value so much in America — I’m tired of politicians who talk about family values and don’t value families.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What we need to do is raise the minimum wage.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We also need to hold on to equal pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Women work for 76 cents on the dollar for the same work that men do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not right in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we had an initiative that we were working on to raise women’s pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve cut it off.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve stopped it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They don’t enforce these kinds of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think that it’s a matter of fundamental right that if we raise the minimum wage, 15 million Americans would be positively affected.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’d put money into the hands of people who work hard, who obey the rules, who play for the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And if we did that, we’d have more consumption ability in America, which is what we need right now in order to kick our economy into gear.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will fight tooth and nail to pass the minimum wage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And as president, I am committed to changing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t care if the idea comes from the other side or this side.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think we have to come together and work to change it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Over 20 years in the United States Senate, I’ve worked with John McCain, who’s sitting here, I’ve worked with other colleagues.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve reached across the aisle.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve tried to find the common ground, because that’s what makes us strong as Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And if Americans trust me with the presidency, I can pledge to you, we will have the most significant effort, openly — not secret meetings in the White House with special interests, not ideologically driven efforts to push people aside — but a genuine effort to try to restore America’s hope and possibilities by bringing people together.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And one of the ways we’re going to do it is, I’m going to work with my friend, John McCain, to further campaign finance reform so we get these incredible amounts of money out of the system and open it up to average people, so America is really represented by the people who make up America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My biggest disappointment in Washington is how partisan the town is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I had a record of working with Republicans and Democrats as the governor of Texas, and I was hopeful I’d be able to do the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we made good progress early on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The No Child Left Behind Act, incredibly enough, was good work between me and my administration and people like Senator Ted Kennedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we worked together with Democrats to relieve the tax burden on the middle class and all who pay taxes in order to make sure this economy continues to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But Washington is a tough town.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the way I view it is there’s a lot of entrenched special interests there, people who are, you know, on one side of the issue or another and they spend enormous sums of money and they convince different senators to taut their way or different congressmen to talk about their issue, and they dig in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll continue, in the four years, to continue to try to work to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent said this is a bitterly divided time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Pretty divided in the 2000 election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So in other words, it’s pretty divided during the 1990s as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re just in a period — we’ve got to work to bring it — my opponent keeps mentioning John McCain, and I’m glad he did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: John McCain is for me for president because he understands I have the right view in winning the war on terror and that my plan will succeed in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And my opponent has got a plan of retreat and defeat in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To listen to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To stand up straight and not scowl.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I love the strong women around me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t tell you how much I love my wife and our daughters.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am — you know it’s really interesting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I tell the people on the campaign trail, when I asked Laura to marry me, she said, “Fine, just so long as I never have to give a speech.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: “I said, “OK, you’ve got a deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: “Fortunately, she didn’t hold me to that deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And she’s out campaigning along with our girls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And she speaks English a lot better than I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think people understand what she’s saying.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But they see a compassionate, strong, great first lady in Laura Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t tell you how lucky I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When I met her in the backyard at Joe and Jan O’Neill’s in Midland, Texas, it was the classic backyard barbecue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: O’Neill said, “Come on over.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think you’ll find somebody who might interest you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: “So I said all right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Bopped over there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There was only four of us there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And not only did she interest me, I guess you would say it was love at first sight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, I guess the president and you and I are three examples of lucky people who married up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And some would say maybe me more so than others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I can take it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Can I say, if I could just say a word about a woman that you didn’t ask about, but my mom passed away a couple years ago, just before I was deciding to run.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And she was in the hospital, and I went in to talk to her and tell her what I was thinking of doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And she looked at me from her hospital bed and she just looked at me and she said, “Remember: integrity, integrity, integrity.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “Those are the three words that she left me with.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And my daughters and my wife are people who just are filled with that sense of what’s right, what’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They also kick me around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They keep me honest.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They don’t let me get away with anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can sometimes take myself too seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They surely don’t let me do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I’m blessed, as I think the president is blessed, as I said last time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve watched him with the first lady, who I admire a great deal, and his daughters.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He’s a great father.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I think we’re both very lucky.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: My fellow Americans, as you heard from Bob Schieffer a moment ago, America is being tested by division.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: More than ever, we need to be united as a country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And, like Franklin Roosevelt, I don’t care whether an idea is a Republican idea or a Democrat idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I just care whether it works for America and whether it’s going to make us stronger.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: These are dangerous times.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe I offer tested, strong leadership that can calm the waters of the troubled world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I believe that we can together do things that are within the grasp of Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can lift our schools up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can create jobs that pay more than the jobs we’re losing overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can have health care for all Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can further the cause of equality in our nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Let me just make it clear: I will never allow any country to have a veto over our security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Just as I fought for our country as a young man, with the same passion I will fight to defend this nation that I love.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And, with faith in God and with conviction in the mission of America, I believe that we can reach higher.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think the greatest possibilities of our country, our dreams and our hopes, are out there just waiting for us to grab onto them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I ask you to embark on that journey with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I ask you for your trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I ask you for your help.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I ask you to allow me the privilege of leading this great nation of ours, of helping us to be stronger here at home and to be respected again in the world and, most of all, to be safer forever.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Goodnight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And God bless the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In the Oval Office, there’s a painting by a friend of Laura and mine named — by Tom Lee.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a West Texas painting, a painting of a mountain scene.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he said this about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He said, “Sarah and I live on the east side of the mountain.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the sunrise side, not the sunset side.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the side to see the day that is coming, not to see the day that is gone.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: “ I love the optimism in that painting, because that’s how I feel about America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve been through a lot together during the last 3 3/4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve come through a recession, a stock market decline, an attack on our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yet, because of the hard work of the American people and good policies, this economy is growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over the next four years, we’ll make sure the economy continues to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We reformed our school system, and now there’s an achievement gap in America that’s beginning to close.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over the next four years, we’ll continue to insist on excellence in every classroom in America so that our children have a chance to realize the great promise of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over the next four years, we’ll continue to work to make sure health care is available and affordable.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over the next four years, we’ll continue to rally the armies of compassion, to help heal the hurt that exists in some of our country’s neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m optimistic that we’ll win the war on terror, but I understand it requires firm resolve and clear purpose.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We must never waver in the face of this enemy that — these ideologues of hate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as we pursue the enemy wherever it exists, we’ll also spread freedom and liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We got great faith in the ability of liberty to transform societies, to convert a hostile world to a peaceful world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My hope for America is a prosperous America, a hopeful America and a safer world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank you for listening tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m asking for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: God bless you.
